description: Server half of XH's Hoist toolkit: a Grails 7 plugin with BaseService and BaseController, managed caches and timers, Hazelcast clustering, config, prefs, roles, monitoring. Pairs with hoist-react.
rules: Every Grails service extends io.xh.hoist.BaseService and every controller extends BaseController (or RestController for CRUD). Bare Grails services and controllers miss lifecycle, logging, identity, and admin integration.

Create caches, cached values, timers, and Hazelcast structures through the BaseService factories (createCache, createCachedValue, createTimer), never directly. In clearCaches() overrides call super.clearCaches() first, then clear each resource.

Read config through configService typed getters (getString, getInt, getBool, getMap, getList, getObject(Class)); never query AppConfig directly. Declare required configs, prefs, and roles with ConfigSpec, PreferenceSpec, and RoleSpec at bootstrap.

Every controller action needs an access annotation (@AccessRequiresRole, @AccessRequiresAnyRole, @AccessRequiresAllRoles, or @AccessAll) on the method or the class. Do not re-check roles inside the action.

Render responses with renderJSON() and read request bodies with parseRequestJSON(); do not use Grails render() or request.JSON. Let exceptions propagate from controller actions instead of wrapping them in try/catch.
Log through the LogSupport methods (logInfo, logDebug, withInfo, withDebug) with varargs and maps, not a raw SLF4J logger. Throw RoutineRuntimeException for expected user-facing errors.
Annotate service methods that touch the database: @ReadOnly for queries and @Transactional for mutations. Avoid N+1 queries.
The xh prefix marks framework-owned configs, preferences, roles, and services; do not use it for application-owned identifiers.

The develop branch documents the unreleased next major. Match the app's hoistCoreVersion: pick that version in Context7, and read docs/upgrade-notes when crossing majors. hoist-react docs/version-compatibility.md lists the paired versions.
